name: Epigenetic Regulation, Chromatin Remodeling, and Genomic Imprinting

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: Histone acetylation by HATs relaxes chromatin (euchromatin), promoting transcription; HDACs reverse this mark
DNA methylation at promoter CpG islands by DNMTs silences transcription by recruiting MeCP2 and corepressors
Rett syndrome is an X-linked dominant disorder caused by de novo loss-of-function mutations in MeCP2
Prader-Willi syndrome results from loss of paternal 15q11-q13 expression, causing neonatal hypotonia and hyperphagia
Angelman syndrome results from loss of maternal 15q11-q13 (UBE3A) expression, manifesting with ataxia and paroxysmal laughter
reference.pathophysiology: Epigenetic modifications regulate transcriptional competence without altering genomic DNA nucleotide sequence. Methylation of promoter CpG islands stabilizes gene silencing. Failure of methyl-CpG-binding protein MeCP2 disrupts neuronal synaptic maturation in Rett syndrome. Imprinting defects or uniparental disomy at 15q11-q13 abolish essential monoallelic gene expression, causing parent-of-origin neurodevelopmental syndromes.
additionalDifferentials: Rett syndrome vs typical autism spectrum disorder
additionalInvestigations: Methylation-specific PCR and MS-MLPA for 15q11-q13 imprinting analysis
Chromosomal microarray for 15q11-q13 microdeletions or uniparental disomy
Sanger or NGS sequencing of the MECP2 gene for Rett syndrome
Bisulfite sequencing for promoter CpG island hypermethylation
